meta.note: Minimal-pair cases for Professor Di Somma's point 2. Each pair gives an AMBIGUOUS description plus two RESOLUTIONS that differ by a single fact about how the output is used. The tool should (a) return needs-info on the ambiguous input with a question that probes how the output is used and who acts on it, and (b) via the clarify loop, update the assessment for each resolution. Two pairs flip the tier; MP3 keeps the tier (high-risk) but changes the sub-provision, facts and rationale — covering both of the professor's scenarios. Derogation variants are boundary cases: the primary check is that the reasoning invokes Art 6(3) and the key_facts reflect the human-review fact; the tier label (minimal-risk) is secondary. Scoring uses the descendant rule (a child/parent id satisfies the expected id). must_reflect phrases are checked case-insensitively against key_facts + rationale.
meta.scoring: ambiguous: tier == needs-info AND clarifying_question mentions how the output is used / who acts on it. resolution: expected_citation present (descendant rule) AND all must_reflect phrases appear in key_facts or rationale. Tier is a secondary check for derogation (minimal-risk) variants.

pairs.ambiguous: We use AI to summarise job applications.
question_must_probe: whether a human reviews the applications / who makes the decision

resolutions.clarification: A recruiter reads every application in full alongside the summary, and the AI does not rank, score or filter candidates.
resolutions.note: Boundary: Annex III(4) area, but the Art 6(3) derogation applies because the summary is a preparatory aid that does not materially influence the decision. Primary check: rationale invokes Art 6(3).

resolutions.clarification: The system also ranks candidates and only the top ten are reviewed by a recruiter.
resolutions.note: Ranking materially influences who is considered, so the derogation does not apply; high-risk under Annex III(4).

pairs.ambiguous: We use AI to review loan applications.
question_must_probe: whether the AI scores or decides

resolutions.clarification: The AI only writes a plain-language summary of each application; a loan officer reads the full application and decides independently.
resolutions.note: Boundary: essential-services area, but a preparatory summary where a human decides from the full file can fall under the Art 6(3) derogation. Primary check: rationale invokes Art 6(3).

resolutions.clarification: The AI assigns each applicant a creditworthiness score that determines whether the loan is approved.
resolutions.note: Credit scoring that determines access to a loan is high-risk under Annex III(5).

pairs.ambiguous: We use AI in our workforce management.
question_must_probe: whether it is for hiring/recruitment or for managing existing employees

resolutions.clarification: It screens and ranks external job applicants to shortlist them for recruiters.
It evaluates current employees' performance to inform promotion and termination decisions.
resolutions.note: Management of workers (promotion/termination/performance): Annex III(4)(b). Same tier as MP3-A, but a different sub-provision, facts and rationale — the professor's 'label stays, explanation changes' case.
